config.aboutPageDescription:
Bacan Malay, or Bacan [btj], is a Malayic language spoken on the island of Bacan in North Maluku province, Indonesia. The data was collected by Professor Gary Holton and adapted into an online dictionary format by Suphitchaya Singsahuth (Fa). The dictionary comprises 4,788 entries.

The orthography used in this dictionary is Latin-based, consisting of 27 characters:

  • 17 consonants — b, c, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, r, s, t, w, y
  • 10 vowels — a, e, i, o, u, á, é, í, ó, ú
Accordingly, the fuzzy search algorithm has been adjusted to assign a lower weight to the distinction between accented and unaccented vowels (0.5) relative to the distinction between a vowel and a consonant. (1.0)

Each entry is structured as follows:

  • Headword
  • Part of Speech
  • Definition
  • Example sentences and translations (up to 5)
  • Scientific Name
  • Grammatical Category
  • Social Context
  • Semantic Domain
  • Language of Origin

There is no subentry at this stage of dictionary development because it is difficult to represent relationships between words as Mother Tongues dictionaries treat each item as an independent unit and provide no documentation specifying how words are to be linked to one another.

The semantic domains represented in this dictionary are: animal, bird, boat, body, clothing, color, culinary, fish, fishing, food, game, geography, health, house, insect, kinship, medicine, mollusc, natural phenomenon, personal name, place name, plant, sago, sailing, sea creature, society, spiritual, tool, tree, and utensil.
